clue.text: Bishop lives in style with a painter like Picasso

indicators.note: one part sits in another, so the first pair of letters goes inside the word for fashion

parts.note: the cut of a garment is its style
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to be or live: 'is' as in exists

explanation.surface: A bishop with a stylish home who keeps company with a famous artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lives' reads as a verb about the bishop's home; here it is just IS, as in 'exists'.
explanation.definitionFit: Picasso co-founded Cubism, so an artist of his school is a Cubist, a member of that movement.

clue.text: An outstanding performer, kind to imitate

parts.note: a class is a kind or category
to act is to pretend or put on an imitation

explanation.surface: A talented performer who is generous towards would-be imitators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' is a noun (type), not the adjective for generous.
explanation.definitionFit: A class act is an informal term for someone of real quality and distinction, especially a performer.

clue.text: Reportedly purchase extra

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than read, so the word comes by its sound

parts.note: to purchase is to buy

explanation.surface: Apparently buying something more on top.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored when the ball passes the batter without being hit, counted as an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: Byes are one kind of cricket extra, runs not credited to the batsman.

clue.text: Supporters after free dish

indicators.note: coming after places the first-named word behind the other

parts.note: spare means free or unused, as in spare time
ribs support the chest and also a boat's hull

explanation.surface: Fans chasing a free meal after the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporters' suggests football fans; here they are the bones that hold up the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare ribs are a dish of pork rib cuts, typically barbecued or cooked in sauce.

clue.text: They help winter sportsmen get to the top

definitions.text: They help winter sportsmen get to the top

parts.words: They help winter sportsmen get to the top
parts.note: surface reading: coaches or sponsors who help athletes reach the top of their sport
setter's reading: literally carried up to the top of a mountain slope

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get to the top' sounds like success in a career; it is literal, a mechanical ride up the slope for skiers.
explanation.definitionFit: These cable or chairlift devices carry skiers uphill, the mountain summit being the literal top.

clue.text: Political advisers back the nine upset about Italian meeting Conservative

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the short pair
something upset is knocked over and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: meeting means joining up, so the two short pieces are put together

parts.note: IT is an abbreviation for Italian
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: Political advisers are backing a group of nine, which upsets the Italian and the Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: BACK THE NINE is rearranged around IT + C.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen cabinet is an informal group of advisers to a leader, outside the official cabinet.

clue.text: There's nothing up with American, Lucy's brother

indicators.note: together with, so the second piece is added on
in a down clue, going up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: nil means nothing
US is short for American, as in US politics

explanation.surface: Nothing is happening with an American, according to his sister Lucy.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Peanuts comic strip, Linus van Pelt (with his security blanket) is the younger brother of bossy Lucy.
explanation.definitionFit: Linus and Lucy van Pelt are siblings in Charles Schulz's Peanuts cartoon strip.

clue.text: I may be seen flying from escort vessel rail, perhaps

parts.note: a frigate is a warship used for escort duty
a rail is a kind of wading bird, an example of the class

explanation.surface: Something spotted flying off the rail of a naval ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The rail looks like a ship's railing; it is a marsh bird. The clue speaks in the answer's own voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The frigatebird is a large tropical seabird known for soaring for long periods over the ocean.

clue.text: Bloodhound in film

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tracking dog (...-hound), hence a detective
second meaning: the 1972 thriller starring Laurence Olivier and Michael Caine

explanation.surface: A tracking dog appears in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1972 film, from Anthony Shaffer's play, is a cat-and-mouse mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleuth is a detective, originally a sleuth-hound or bloodhound that tracks by scent; it is also a film title.

clue.text: Unstable country in Caribbean? Plan changed about university

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go around the single letter
changed letters are altered in order to make something new

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A shaky Caribbean nation changes its plans for a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caribbean' seems part of the definition but its letters are the fodder, with PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana republic is a politically unstable small state, often reliant on one export crop like bananas.

clue.text: Sphere of intense activity in district around the north

indicators.note: one word goes around another, wrapping the compass letter inside it

parts.note: a district is an area
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Describing some busy neighbourhood up north where much is going on.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively an arena is a field or scene of conflict and lively activity, like the political arena.

clue.text: Listening carefully in shelter absorbed by musical, after retiring

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken in, so the shelter word sits inside the other
retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the musical's name is read from the end

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Perón
a tent is a simple shelter

explanation.surface: Someone attending carefully to a show while sheltering, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical; 'retiring' looks like shyness but signals reading it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Being attentive means paying close heed, the state of someone listening with care.

clue.text: English person , a head, appearing with answer back in school

indicators.note: the reversed group is placed inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: SCH is an abbreviation for school

indicators.note: going back means the joined pieces are read from right to left
appearing alongside, so the pieces are placed next to each other

parts.note: taken as written
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Orford Ness
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: An Englishman and a headteacher seem to be replying to someone at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' suggests a headteacher at the school; it is a headland, the sense in place names like Orford Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassenach is a Scots (and Irish) term, often mildly derogatory, for an English person.

clue.text: Get on well initially using a piece of gymnastic equipment

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the second-named piece is placed in front

parts.note: a spring is a natural well or water source
to board a bus or ship is to get on it

explanation.surface: Advice to make a good start in life by using gym apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get on well' reads as a phrase about thriving; split it into 'Get on' and 'well', with 'initially' putting the well first.
explanation.definitionFit: A springboard is the flexible board gymnasts bounce from to launch vaults and leaps.

clue.text: Leader in stock market is astute

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of stock
a mart is a market

explanation.surface: The top performer on the stock exchange is a shrewd operator.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart and astute are synonyms, both meaning clever and quick to judge situations.

clue.text: One is one church dignitary with less feeling

indicators.note: together with, so the two words are placed side by side

parts.note: surface padding: the article reads naturally but adds no letters
a cardinal is a senior Catholic churchman
more numb, i.e. having less feeling

explanation.surface: A senior cleric is said to be emotionally colder than others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is read as numb-er, comparative of numb, not the noun. 'One' looks like a pronoun but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting numbers like one, two and three are cardinal numbers, as distinct from ordinals like first.

clue.text: Beginning to make high teas with pâté spread

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: the first letter of make

indicators.note: high means intoxicated, so these letters are in a disorderly state

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written without the accents, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Starting to prepare high teas by spreading pâté on bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High teas' reads as a phrase (a British early-evening meal) but 'high' is the anagram signal and 'spread' is the definition, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat paste is a savoury sandwich spread made of finely ground cooked meat.

clue.text: Dull policeman's round gets one exhausted

definitions.note: noun phrase: a deadbeat, someone worn out or a down-and-out

parts.note: dead can mean dull or lifeless, as a dead colour
a constable's beat is the area he patrols

explanation.surface: A boring police patrol leaves an officer worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead-beat means utterly tired, so a deadbeat is a worn-out or idle person.

clue.text: Gradually, video's run back in new maisonette

indicators.note: a recording run back is rewound, so the word is read from its end
the reversed recording word is placed inside the rearranged dwelling
a new version of a word reorders its letters

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a video is a tape

explanation.surface: Someone rewinding a video at home in a new flat.
explanation.walkthrough: A maisonette is a flat on two floors. 'Run back' reads as rewinding the video, and that is just what happens to the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something gradually means doing it slowly in stages, step by step.

clue.text: Forbid question on old Shakespearean general

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so they join in order

parts.note: to ban is to forbid
QU is an abbreviation for question
O is an abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to answer questions about an old Shakespeare commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Banquo is a Scottish general in Macbeth, murdered on Macbeth's orders and returning as a ghost.

clue.text: Collection of photographs showing wild laburnum with no vase

indicators.note: wild letters run out of control and land in a new order
without something means that portion is removed from the shrub's name

parts.note: taken as written
an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: Pictures of a wild laburnum tree, but none of a flower vase.
explanation.walkthrough: Take URN out of LABURNUM to leave LABUM, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a book for keeping photographs, stamps or similar items together.

clue.text: Girl, first to mime song

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so that alone is kept

parts.note: the first letter of mime
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A girl is the first to mime along to a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is a girl's given name; crosswords often use 'girl' for any female first name.

clue.text: One politician comes into Dundee, amazingly not delayed

indicators.note: entering a place means going inside it, so these letters sit within the Scottish city's
something amazing is astonishing and transformed, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written, then rearranged
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A politician arrives in the Scottish city of Dundee, surprisingly on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Unimpeded means unhindered or unobstructed, so nothing has held it back or slowed it.

clue.text: Trouble during first half of reel after square dance

indicators.note: something happening during an event is inside it, so one piece sits within the other
only the opening half is kept, so the back half of the word is dropped
coming after means following, so the second piece comes behind the first

parts.note: a quad is a quadrangle, a square courtyard
taken as written, then halved
ill as a noun means harm or trouble

explanation.surface: A problem arises midway through a Scottish reel, after a square dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A reel is a lively Scottish dance, which makes 'square dance' look like the definition; 'square' is the courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: The quadrille is an old French square dance for four couples.

clue.text: To pick off soldiers, say, keep inside houses after revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the found letters are read backwards
a phrase that houses something holds it within, so the letters are found spanning the words

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: In a revolution, troops are shot at while people stay indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keEP INSide' holds EPINS; reversed, it gives the answer. 'Keep' and 'inside' look like an instruction but are just the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To snipe is to shoot at people from a hidden position, typically picking off individual soldiers.

clue.text: One representative of a mischievous child

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
an MP is an elected parliamentary representative

explanation.surface: Someone who acts as a spokesman for a naughty youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: An imp is a small devil, and by extension a playful, naughty little child.

clue.text: One leaves order for heavy guns and military supplies

indicators.note: when something leaves it departs, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: an ordinance is an authoritative order or decree
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A soldier departs with an order to fetch artillery and supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I from ORDINANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance means artillery and also military stores and equipment generally.

clue.text: Dictator in terminal receiving head of state

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the selected letter goes inside the terminal word

parts.note: a depot is a bus or rail terminal

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of state

explanation.surface: A tyrant at an airport or station welcomes a visiting head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a ruler with absolute power, the same as a dictator or tyrant.
